question: Identify the correct formula to find the potential difference between two points.
solution:
The correct answer is **V=W/Q**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The electric potential difference is the difference in electric potential (V) between the final and the initial location when work is done upon a charge to change its potential energy.
 
• The potential difference between two points is equal to the work done in moving a unit of positive charge from one point to the other.
 
 
• **V = W/Q (V = potential difference, W = work done, Q = charge)**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The electric potential difference between two points in an electric circuit carrying some current is the work done to move a unit charge from one point to another.
 
• Thus, a potential difference is the work done per unit charge and is given as V =W/Q.
